name: nofp
description: FP trap stubs and the libm wrap surface for FPU-less guests
note: The zkVM platforms link these wraps. The stock musl target also links module.o (bflat.csproj puts a copy in lib/linux/riscv64/musl), but without the wraps.

wrap.note: libm: divert the math surface referenced by the runtime (MathHelpers.cpp RhpDbl* helpers, GC allocation sampling) to the nofp trap stubs. The bundled musl is built rv64im, so its implementations would link and run correctly - the point is that a transcendental has no business inside a proof, and a guest that reaches one is a bug worth hearing about. fmod and fmodf are deliberately NOT here: they are the C# % operator on double and float, ordinary arithmetic the language defines, and musl's are integer-only.
musl fmt_fp dependency, see nofp module

asprintf is referenced only by the PAL's CGroup CPU-limit parsing, which cannot open its /proc//sys inputs on zisk (pal's open() returns -1). The stub returns -1 (the documented asprintf failure mode) and, more importantly, keeps musl's vasprintf/fmt_fp/scalbn members - hard-float F/D code - out of the link.
